facts.quote:
government experts primarily receive the testing 
data that developers choose to share.
facts.summary: The preliminary assessment identifies an information imbalance in AI safety validation: developers largely design their own evaluations, making standardized independent assessment and better-resourced measurement important capacity needs.

facts.quote:
many 
decisions about training data, safeguards, 
deployment thresholds, model access and 
capability release sit inside private firms.
facts.summary: The report links concentrated AI inputs and business-led frontier development to private control over important governance choices. Its numerical development and compute comparisons are explicitly dated to 2025.
facts.document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment using dated 2025 evidence; not current speech counts.

facts.quote:
Inclusion requires targeted 
investment, public data sets and benchmark 
initiatives for underrepresented linguistic and 
cultural contexts
facts.summary: The report identifies linguistic inclusion and more geographically representative evaluation as capacity needs, observing that evidence is concentrated in high-income English-language settings.

facts.quote:
Multi-
stakeholder financing, including the Global Fund on AI 
proposed by the UN Secretary-General, may help.
facts.summary: The report presents pooled data, capital, compute, energy and talent as possible responses to dependence on foreign AI infrastructure, and refers to the Global Fund as a proposal rather than an established funding mechanism.
facts.document_status: Preliminary scientific report describing a financing proposal.

facts.quote:
Building national and regional AI 
safety institutes and technical secondments 
for regulators may help to build capacity.
facts.summary: National and regional safety institutes, regulator secondments and evaluation adapted to low-resource languages are presented as possible ways to strengthen governance capacity.
facts.document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment of possible capacity measures; not an adopted mandate.

facts.quote:
Governments have 
committed to promoting AI literacy in the Global 
Digital Compact
facts.summary: The report places AI literacy alongside institutional capacity, data, training, regulation and workflow redesign as necessary complements to access, and cites a literacy commitment in the Global Digital Compact.
facts.document_status: Preliminary scientific report referring to the Global Digital Compact commitment.
